answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before earning, and to build reputation only through verified completed work. The stake is a bridge between past behaviour and present privilege: a new identity starts with no trust and earns only a trickle of nectar-like rewards, while a long-lived identity accumulates a visible plume of successful attestations from independent peers. An attacker splitting stake across many fakes dilutes each one's earning power and risks slashing on every identity, so mass fakery costs more than it returns.
